segmentRevenue.title: Revenue by segment
segmentRevenue.content:
Quanta reports two segments since FY2024: Electric (transmission, distribution and substation work for utilities, plus the renewable-energy and underground-transmission infrastructure that feeds AI data-center power demand) and Underground Utility & Infrastructure (gas distribution, pipeline and broadband/fiber work -- the smaller, legacy segment). Periods before FY2024 used a three-segment split (Electric Power / Underground & Infrastructure / Renewable Energy) and are not shown here to avoid mixing definitions.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: Electric is ~82% of group revenue and is growing faster than Underground -- the data-center and grid-reliability capex cycle shows up almost entirely in this line, not the group total.

What to watch:

  • Electric's share of total revenue widening further
  • Underground segment growth stalling while Electric accelerates (confirms the mix shift is demand-driven, not just segment reclassification)

segmentOperatingIncome.title: Operating income by segment
segmentOperatingIncome.content:
Segment operating income before the unallocated Corporate overhead line. Shows which segment is actually generating the group's profit growth, as opposed to just its revenue growth.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: Electric's operating income has grown faster than its revenue in recent quarters -- margin expansion on top of volume growth, consistent with pricing power in a capacity-constrained grid-buildout market. Underground's operating income is choppier and smaller in absolute terms.

What to watch:

  • Electric margin (operating income / SegmentRevenue_Electric) trending up, not just the dollar figure
  • Underground profitability stabilizing versus continuing to lag its own revenue growth

segmentBacklog.title: Backlog by segment
segmentBacklog.content:
Backlog is signed, awarded work not yet recognized as revenue -- the forward order book. Shown per segment because Electric's backlog has grown much faster than Underground's, telegraphing where future revenue growth will concentrate before it shows up in the income statement.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: Electric backlog has roughly doubled across FY2024-FY2026 (the AI/data-center power buildout showing up as signed work), while Underground backlog has grown far more slowly off a smaller base.

What to watch:

  • Backlog growth outpacing or lagging revenue growth by segment (a leading signal either way)
  • Electric backlog concentration risk -- a large book depends on a narrower set of utility/hyperscaler customers than the more fragmented Underground segment

balanceSheet.title: Balance sheet
balanceSheet.content:
Shareholders' equity is assets less liabilities; plotted against total liabilities to show leverage.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: equity that grows only through revaluations or share issues is not the same as retained earnings.

What to watch:

  • Liabilities growing faster than equity
  • Goodwill share of equity after acquisitions

cashDebt.title: Cash and debt
cashDebt.content:
Cash & equivalents against total borrowings (leases excluded unless noted).

For Quanta Services, Inc.: the DCF's net-debt bridge uses these balances at the latest balance-sheet date.

What to watch:

  • Net debt trend versus EBITDA
  • Refinancing dates and covenants in the filings

epsDps.title: EPS and dividends
epsDps.content:
EPS is net income per share; DPS is the cash dividend paid per share. Both are in major currency units.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: the payout ratio (DPS / EPS) shows how much of earnings is returned versus reinvested.

What to watch:

  • EPS growth versus net income growth (dilution)
  • Dividends funded from earnings, not debt

fcf.title: Free cash flow
fcf.content:
Reported FCF is operating cash flow less capital expenditure. Owner FCF (from the DCF) further deducts stock-based compensation, interest income and lease principal -- the cash an owner could actually take out.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: the gap between net income and owner FCF is the earnings-quality question the valuation is built on.

What to watch:

  • FCF persistently below net income
  • Working-capital swings inflating one year's FCF

margins.title: Margins
margins.content:
Gross margin is revenue less cost of revenue; operating margin deducts operating expenses; net margin is after interest and tax.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: the spread between gross and operating margin is the cost of running the business; a widening spread with flat gross margin means opex is growing faster than sales.

What to watch:

  • Direction of operating margin over several years, not one
  • One-offs (impairments, disposals) that distort net margin

ocfCapex.title: Operating cash flow and CapEx
ocfCapex.content:
Operating cash flow is cash generated by operations; CapEx is cash invested in fixed and intangible assets.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: CapEx here is shown as stored (sign convention varies by ticker); the DCF splits it into stay-in-business and growth where disclosed.

What to watch:

  • CapEx rising faster than revenue
  • OCF that diverges from EBITDA

profit.title: Profit lines
profit.content:
Gross profit is revenue less cost of revenue; operating income deducts operating expenses; net income is after interest, tax and one-offs.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: the three lines together show where margin is made and lost between the top line and the bottom.

What to watch:

  • Operating income growing slower than gross profit (opex creep)
  • Net income far from operating income (interest, tax, one-offs)

revenue.title: Revenue
revenue.content:
Revenue is the top line: what customers paid for goods and services in the period, before any costs.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: the growth rate matters more than the level; compare it with the DCF's base-case growth path below.

What to watch:

  • Acceleration or deceleration in YoY growth
  • Whether growth is organic or acquired
  • Interim rows show seasonality

sbc.title: Stock-based compensation and share count
sbc.content:
Stock-based comp is the expense of equity awards; shares outstanding shows the dilution it causes net of buybacks.

For Quanta Services, Inc.: the DCF charges SBC as a cash cost and holds the share count flat, so this chart is the check on that assumption.

What to watch:

  • Share count rising while buybacks are advertised
  • SBC as a percentage of revenue
